newsitem.title: USA: BRISTOL-MYERS WINS BREAST IMPLANT CASE.
newsitem.headline: BRISTOL-MYERS WINS BREAST IMPLANT CASE.

text.p: A jury returned a verdict in favor of Bristol-Myers Squibb Co and its Medical Engineering Corp unit Wednesday in a breast implant case in northern California, Bristol-Myers Squibb said.
The company said a Sonoma County Superior Court jury rejected the allegations of plaintiff Deborah Stirling that her breast implants had caused a variety of ailments.
Stirling, 47, received Surgitec breast implants made by Medical Engineering Corp in 1985 following a mastectomy for cancer. In 1992, her right implant was removed.

Stirling alleged she had an autoimmune disease, that her breast implant had ruptured and that she had been defrauded because she was not told of the risk of rupture, according to Kevin Dunne, an attorney for Bristol-Myers Squibb.
He said the jury found in favor of the companies on three causes of action stated in Stirling's suit -- liability, negligence and fraud -- after a six-week trial.
The lawsuit did not state how much Stirling was seeking in damages but it would have been millions of dollars, Dunne said.
Lawyers for Stirling could not immediately be reached for comment.

"Juries have consistently rejected claims by plaintiffs that breast implants cause systemic disease. They have recognized these claims are not supported by scrupulous and reliable science," said John McGoldrick, senior vice president and general counsel of Bristol-Myers Squibb.
